title: Tenali and the Two Liars

full_text:
Two professional boasters from rival provinces, Shankara and Narayana, met at a festival in Vijayanagara and began competing over who could tell the most outrageous falsehood without blinking.
Shankara boasted:
'Last year, I planted a pumpkin seed in my garden. Within three days, it grew into an enormous pumpkin so colossal that three hundred cavalry soldiers pitched their tents inside it during a rainstorm!'

Narayana scoffed:
'That is nothing! My grandfather was a coppersmith who cast an enormous bronze cooking cauldron so vast that two thousand blacksmiths hammered inside it for twenty years, and the sound of the hammers on one side could not be heard on the other!'

Shankara frowned, suspicious:
'Narayana, why on earth would anyone cast such a ridiculous, impossible bronze cauldron?'

Narayana smirked:
'Why, Shankara? To cook your colossal pumpkin, of course!'

The surrounding crowd laughed, declaring Narayana the winner.
Puffed up with pride, the two boasters turned to Tenali Raman, who was standing nearby:
'Hey, Tenali! They say thou art the greatest wit in the empire. Canst thou tell a lie greater than ours?'

Tenali Raman shook his head with grave, solemn dignity:
'Alas, brothers! I cannot participate in your contest, for in all my forty years of life, I have never spoken a single lie, nor have I ever exaggerated by half a syllable!
Every word that passes my lips is pure, unblemished, absolute truth!'

The two boasters stared at Tenali in stunned silence.
Narayana cried: 'What? A court jester who has never spoken a lie in forty years? That is the most monstrous, impossible, colossal lie ever spoken in the history of the world!'

Tenali smiled with effortless brilliance:
'Aha! Then by your own unanimous admission, my lie is far greater than your pumpkin and your cauldron combined! Hand over the championship prize!'

The entire crowd roared with unstoppable laughter.
The two boasters blushed crimson, realized they had been completely outmaneuvered by Tenali’s razor-sharp paradoxical wit, surrendered their prize purse, and slipped away into the crowd, proving that boasting cannot withstand true intelligence.
moral: Outlandish boasting defeats itself when met with an even greater claim of absolute truth.

Acting in hasty anger without listening
